We need answer only JSON. Need extract claims from review. Need adhere schema. Review text: "Trash 👎\nLiteral piece of trash. Never worked. Never fully charged. Hell The damn thing didn’t even stick in the wall I had to put tape on it take it to stick in the outlet!!!!"

We need identify product-review semantic claims, zero/multiple. Each claim exactly one valid primary/secondary taxonomy pair, polarity, evidence_span exact continuous substring from SOURCE_TEXT. Don't infer sentiment from star rating. No invent. Need output {"claims":[...]}.

We parse claims:
- "Never worked." likely reliability_durability / stopped_working? or general_durability? "Never worked" implies stopped_working? It never worked, product doesn't function. Taxonomy reliability_durability includes stopped_working. Primary reliability_durability, secondary stopped_working. Polarity negative. evidence_span exact "Never worked." or "Never worked". Need exact continuous substring. Source has "Never worked." with period. Use "Never worked." maybe includes period. OK.
- "Never fully charged." This is function_performance / charging_success? It's about charging success. "Never fully charged" means charging unsuccessful/incomplete. Primary function_performance, secondary charging_success. Polarity negative. evidence_span "Never fully charged." exact.
- "The damn thing didn’t even stick in the wall I had to put tape on it take it to stick in the outlet!!!!" This is about not sticking in wall/outlet, needed tape to stick in outlet. It likely compatibility_fit / wall_socket_fit? "didn’t even stick in the wall" and "stick in the outlet" indicates plug doesn't stay in wall socket / wall_socket_fit. Primary compatibility_fit, secondary wall_socket_fit. Polarity negative. Evidence span exact: "The damn thing didn’t even stick in the wall I had to put tape on it take it to stick in the outlet!!!!" Need exact continuous substring from SOURCE_TEXT. Check text: "Hell The damn thing didn’t even stick in the wall I had to put tape on it take it to stick in the outlet!!!!" We can include maybe entire sentence. Note there is curly apostrophe in didn’t? Source has "didn’t" with U+2019? The text shows "didn’t" likely curly. We must copy exact. We'll include from "The damn thing..." to end. Could also split "didn’t even stick in the wall" and "take it to stick in the outlet" but same claim. Need exact continuous. evidence_span: "The damn thing didn’t even stick in the wall I had to put tape on it take it to stick in the outlet!!!!" Ensure exact includes "Hell " before? We can start at "The". It is continuous substring: "The damn thing..." yes.
- "Literal piece of trash." This is general negative perhaps other_unknown/uncategorized? It's not a product claim? It's just insult. Could be general performance? "Trash" not specific. We should not invent. Maybe no claim. "Trash 👎" title not source_text? source_text includes "Trash 👎\nLiteral piece of trash." We could ignore because no specific product attribute. The instruction if no supported product claim. But "Literal piece of trash" maybe product quality material_build_quality? Not necessarily. Better not extract.
Need consider "Never worked." Could be reliability_durability stopped_working. "Never fully charged." could also function_performance charging_success. "didn’t even stick in the wall" might be compatibility_fit wall_socket_fit. Also "take it to stick in the outlet" means plug doesn't stay in outlet. Yes.

Need ensure taxonomy pairs valid: primary topic and secondary from allowed list. Any secondary allowed? Schema just enum all secondaries, but ideally secondary should belong to primary? The taxonomy pairs indicate primary/secondary, we should choose valid pair. For stopped_working belongs reliability_durability. charging_success belongs function_performance. wall_socket_fit belongs compatibility_fit.

Need polarity negative for all. "Never worked." negative. "Never fully charged." negative. "didn’t even stick..." negative.

Need evidence spans exact substrings. The full source_text: "Trash 👎\nLiteral piece of trash. Never worked. Never fully charged. Hell The damn thing didn’t even stick in the wall I had to put tape on it take it to stick in the outlet!!!!"

Potential issue: source_text contains newline after 👎. JSON can include newline escaped but evidence spans don't include newline. Fine.

Evidence span for "Never worked.": exact substring "Never worked." yes.
"Never fully charged.": exact substring "Never fully charged." yes.
Third: exact substring starting "The damn thing..." Let's verify apostrophe: source_text in prompt: "didn’t" — the character is U+2019 right single quotation mark. I need output exact. I can copy from prompt. In JSON, can include Unicode. I'll copy "didn’t". It appears as "didn’t" with curly. Need exact. The rest: "The damn thing didn’t even stick in the wall I had to put tape on it take it to stick in the outlet!!!!" Yes.

Could there be another claim: "Hell" no. "Trash" no. If we include "Literal piece of trash" as product_quality/material_build_quality? It's subjective general insult, not material build quality. Not extract.

Need final JSON only. Ensure no markdown. Use exact schema. 
But wait, "Never fully charged" could be about charging_success or charging_speed? It's success: not fully charged = charging_success. Good.
"Never worked" could be general_performance? Taxonomy has reliability_durability stopped_working. "Never worked" = never functioned. stopped_working is more specific, but "never worked" not necessarily stopped after working; but stopped_working implies failure. I think okay. Could also be reliability_durability general_durability. But we choose stopped_working. 
Potential "didn’t even stick in the wall" could be compatibility_fit/port_fit? The physical plug fit into outlet/wall? wall_socket_fit. Good.

Need include claims array. 
Final.

{"claims":[{"primary_topic":"reliability_durability","secondary_topic":"stopped_working","polarity":"negative","evidence_span":"Never worked."},{"primary_topic":"function_performance","secondary_topic":"charging_success","polarity":"negative","evidence_span":"Never fully charged."},{"primary_topic":"compatibility_fit","secondary_topic":"wall_socket_fit","polarity":"negative","evidence_span":"The damn thing didn’t even stick in the wall I had to put tape on it take it to stick in the outlet!!!!"}]}
